_doc: DR. GRABOW dating cabinet (#35, Wave E, built 2026-07-17-eve; roster #41). The great American drugstore pipe — and one of the best-documented: Russell McKay's ad-dated timeline + model-name lists (BOTH mirrored as dedicated pipedia guides). Dating spine: the Linkman->Dr.Grabow name ladder, logo/emblem evolution (shield->spade), the Ajustomatic stem cliff (1949), the Chicago->Sparta NC move (~1952-55), and ad-dated line floors. SOURCES: staging/pipedia/Dr__Grabow_Pipe_History_Timeline.json (McKay/Bridges chronology) + Dr__Grabow_Models__Series_Line__Names_Through_the_Years.json (McKay) + Dr__Grabow.json + RJR_Grabow_information.json + The_Legend_of_Dr__Grabow.json (unread — future). McKay flags much as working-notes -> soft edges get approx/low.

history_anchors._doc: 1892 Louis B. Linkman founds M. LINKMAN & CO, Chicago. 1914 first patent (1104203, aluminum push-stem). 1922 factory at Fullerton & Racine. 1924 stinger patent 1487867. 1930 (or 1931) Linkman starts using the DR. GRABOW name (a real Chicago physician, Paul E. Grabow, d.1965 aged 97). 1933 threaded-stem stinger patent 1896800 (types L1/L2). 1937 'Pre-Smoked' marketing begins (registered 1947). 1941 'C'-cut stinger + PLAIN BLOCK printed logo (LIFE ad). 1942-43 wartime: yellow/orange plastic bands + non-metallic stingers. Oct-1943 block lettering w/o 'Linkman's'; SHIELD emblem on DeLuxe (ads 1943-1946). Late 1944: 'Slanted Blocks' logo + name change to DR. GRABOW PIPE CO + SPADE emblem first in ads + postal zone '14' in addresses. 1946 Lavietes files AJUSTOMATIC patent (granted Feb-1949, #2461905; his D&P Pipe Co had moved to Boone NC 1943 -> the NC connection). 1947 'Dr Grabow' + 'Pre-Smoked' trademarks registered; 'Slanted Block and Oval' logo appears. 1949 brief unionization (ads May-Nov 1949). ~1952-55: Linkman retires; DR. GRABOW RELOCATES TO NORTH CAROLINA (1955 RTDA lists HL&T of NC as maker; 'transition period' pipes = both plants, collector nickname 'Dr. Crapos'). 1957 Linkman dies. Owners ladder: HL&T -> 1985 merge w/ Mastercraft + Sparta Pipes = SPARTA INDUSTRIES (trademark assigned 1987) -> 1997 Sparta merges w/ LANE Ltd -> 1999 Lane->RJ Reynolds -> 2006 International Pipes & Accessories buys Dr. Grabow + Sparta. RJR-era special-offer pipes: Westbrook, Belvedere, Sculptura, Commodore. Line names of the NC era = 1950s-60s CAR names (Eldorado, Viscount, Starfire, Regal, Savoy, Riviera, Lark).

brand_marks.physical: Ladder of tells: MLC-in-oval + 2-digit shape = earliest Dr. Grabow era (c.1930-32). 'Fashioned by Linkman' / Linkman's wording = pre-1945. SHIELD emblem (DeLuxe) = ads 1943-46. SPADE emblem = late-1944 onward (the lasting mark). PLAIN BLOCK logo 1941+, SLANTED BLOCKS late-1944+, SLANTED BLOCK+OVAL 1947+. Push-stem Linkman's vs AJUSTOMATIC threaded system = 1949+. Wartime: colored plastic bands, non-metal stingers. Meerschaum-lined: 'Italy' + no spade = pre-1989, spade + no Italy = post-1989.

table.note: Italian-made Grabows: Lark + 'Little' Duke imported 1964-1984; Meerschaum-Lined from M. Gasparini stamped 'Italy' until 1989 (then Sparta-made w/ spade)

line_years._notes: Floors = McKay's FIRST-AD dates (strong): Westbrook c1955 RJR pipe, ran 'to about 1985 or so' -> [1955,1985]. standard: Mar-1954 ad -> ~1956 replacement window BUT a 'Fashioned by Linkman' 4-digit example exists (McKay calls the name a mystery) -> LOW, narrow kept w/ this caveat. regal Nov-1956 ($2.50) · savoy Oct-1956 · starfire Dec-1956 · riviera Mar-1957 · viscount Dec-1957 ($5) · eldorado Nov-1961 ad but a $10 pipe existed 1956 -> floor 1960 approx · belvedere c1955 (early RJR; later dropped, end unknown) · commodore 1964 ad · golden duke Dec-1964 ad · duke/berwyck c1964 · sculptura 1967 (big-blast sandblast era 1967-69) · color viscount 1971 (brochure-dated) · omega: purchased June-1974 (Amash) -> floor 1974 · CDL 1975-1983 test-market window (EXACT, first in 1976 RTDA) · pacer/viking pacer 1976 (RTDA ad) · royalton 1988 (reused old HL&T name + leftover HLT shield stamp!) · bucko/hillcrest/freehand c1985-91 era. ENDS mostly open (lines ran long) -> 2026 unless documented. NOT encoded: viking (c1960 'or earlier', 1954 patent design — too fuzzy), lark (1964 import but name reused), emperor/alpha/bard/big pipe/cardinal/half-and-half/redwood/vanroy (Lane-era or single-sighting), old Linkman series numbers (Courtleigh 91, De Luxe 92/97/98/99, Ventilator 63-65 etc. = c1937 catalog codes, NOT stamped on pipes per TED's note).

table.label: Linkman wording = Chicago eras (company renamed Dr. Grabow Pipe Co late 1944, but 'Fashioned by Linkman' lingered into the transition) -> wide to the NC handover
MLC-in-oval + plain 2-digit shape = the first Dr. Grabow era (c.1930-32, slack to 1935)
SHIELD emblem (DeLuxe) = ads Oct-1943 to 1946 (+slack). EXCEPTION: 1988 Royalton reused an old HLT shield stamp — check line name
SPADE emblem = late-1944 onward (the enduring Dr. Grabow mark)
push-stem = Linkman construction (pre-Ajustomatic; NC-era VanRoy revival also push -> LOW)
yellow/orange plastic band + non-metallic stinger = the wartime window (1942-43 ads, steel-penny era)
